{{Short description|Field in algebra}}
{{no footnotes|date=September 2026}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Golod–Shafarevich theorem''' is a result in non-commutative [[homological algebra]] which solves the '''class field tower problem''' by showing that [[Hilbert class field|class field]] towers can be infinite. It is named after [[Evgeny Golod]] and [[Igor Shafarevich]], who proved it in 1964.

== Statement of the inequality ==
Let <math>A=K\langle x_1,\dots,x_n\rangle</math> be the [[free algebra]] over a [[field (mathematics)|field]] <math>K</math> in <math>n=d+1</math> non-commuting variables, and let <math>J</math> be the two-sided [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] of <math>A</math> generated by [[homogeneous polynomial|homogeneous]] elements <math>f_j</math> of <math>A</math> of degree <math>d_j</math> with

:<math>2\leq d_1\leq d_2\leq \cdots</math>

where <math>d_j</math> tends to infinity. Let <math>r_i</math> be the number of <math>d_j</math> equal to <math>i</math>, for all <math>i\geq 2</math>.

Let <math>B = A/J</math>; this is a [[graded algebra]]. Let <math>b_j=\dim B_j</math>. <!--What is B_j??--> 
The ''fundamental inequality'' of Golod and Shafarevich states that

:<math> b_j\geq nb_{j-1} -\sum_{i=2}^{j} b_{j-i} r_i.</math>

for all <math>j</math>. As a consequence, <math>B</math> is infinite-dimensional if <math>r_i \leq d^2/4</math> for all <math>i\geq 2</math>.

==Applications==
This result has important applications in [[combinatorial group theory]]:

* If <math>G</math> is a non-trivial finite [[p-group|{{math|''p''}}-group]], then <math>r > d^2/4</math>, where <math>d = \dim H^1(G,\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})</math> and <math>r = \dim H^2(G,\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})</math> (the mod <math>p</math> [[group cohomology|cohomology groups]] of <math>G</math>). In particular, if <math>G</math> is a finite <math>p</math>-group with minimal number of generators <math>d</math> and has <math>r</math> relators in a given presentation, then <math>r > d^2/4</math>.

* For each prime <math>p</math>, there is an infinite group <math>G</math> generated by three elements in which each element has order a power of <math>p</math>. The group <math>G</math> provides a [[counterexample]] to the [[Burnside's problem|generalised Burnside conjecture]]: it is a [[Finitely generated group|finitely generated]] infinite [[torsion group]], although there is no uniform bound on the order of its elements.

=== Class field theory ===

In [[class field theory]], the '''class field [[tower of fields|tower]]''' of a [[number field]] is created by iterating the [[Hilbert class field]] construction. The class field tower problem asks whether this tower is always finite. A consequence of the Golod–Shafarevich theorem is that such towers may be [[infinite tower of fields|infinite]] (in other words, do not always terminate in a field equal to its [[David Hilbert|Hilbert]] class field). Specifically, if <math>K</math> is an [[Quadratic field|imaginary quadratic field]] whose [[Discriminant of an algebraic number field|discriminant]] has at least six prime factors, then the maximal [[splitting of prime ideals in Galois extensions|unramified]] 2-extension of <math>K</math> has infinite [[degree of a field extension|degree]].

More generally, a number field with sufficiently many prime factors in the discriminant has an infinite class field tower.
